local.yahoo.com listing: phone repeated 5x, no email field found via regex scan of full page source.

Facebook page facebook.com/alejandrotattoousa/about: page returned a near-empty response (1542 bytes), consistent with Facebook's login wall blocking unauthenticated scraping; could not verify an About/Contact email this way.

A WebSearch AI-generated summary claimed the Facebook page lists 'alejandrotattoousa@gmail.com', but this could not be independently verified in any fetched page source (raw HTML, Booksy, directory listings). Per pipeline rule against inventing data, this unverified claim was NOT used; email is recorded as null rather than trusting an unconfirmed secondary summary.

Domain checks: alejandrotattoousa.com, alejandrotattoo.com, alejandrotattoobodypiercing.com, alejandrotattooandbodypiercing.com all return connection failures (curl exit/HTTP 000), confirming no owned domain and therefore no domain-based email guess is safe either.
Conclusion: no public, independently-verifiable email found after exhausting all listed sources. Outreach relies on phone (call/text) and Instagram DM as the manual channels.

language_detection: Instagram bio and captions are in English (e.g. 'More than ink. It's art.'). Of 3 named Booksy reviews with authors, 2 are in English and 1 (Alessandra O.) is in Spanish, reflecting Orlando's bilingual market; page defaults to English with a working ES/EN toggle covering both audiences.
brand_vibe: Black background with gold/champagne serif wordmark ('ALEJANDRO' in Playfair-style gold caps), luxury positioning language ('Luxury in every detail', 'More than ink, it's art', 'Luxury Piercings - Premium Jewelry - Since 1998') consistent across every one of the business's own promotional graphics found in the Booksy gallery. This matches templates/dark-v2's existing black/gold palette almost exactly, so the palette was kept as-is rather than re-derived, since it is already true to the real brand.

sources_checked: scripts/booksy_dossier.py + booksy_gallery.py: downloaded 16 images (bk-1..bk-16) from the Booksy business gallery.

Instagram web_profile_info for @alejandrotattoousa: first 12 timeline posts are ALL GraphVideo (Reels) with heavy permanent text/logo overlays baked into the video poster frames (aftercare tips, booking CTAs, before/after slides); none of the 12 poster thumbnails were clean enough to use without significant crop loss, except one (dragon shoulder tattoo) which was cropped as a trial but ultimately dropped for still showing partial text at every crop tested.
Facebook: page fetch blocked by login wall (1542 byte response), no photos retrievable without authentication.
photos.curation_notes: Every downloaded photo was visually reviewed via the contact sheet (_sheet.jpg) and individually before selection. Excluded from gallery entirely: bk-6 (face piercing close-up with visibly red/irritated skin and a closed eye, prohibited per quality gate), bk-4 and bk-5 (pure marketing/product graphic cards with no real finished-work photo, tongue-out close-up portrait), bk-8 (cluttered marketing collage with a mid-session insert photo and comparison markup lines), bk-11 (cluttered two-panel collage with logo overlay and a second inset close-up, no clean crop possible), bk-2 (small circular logo badge, used only as the small nav/footer/favicon avatar, never as a gallery tile), bk-1 (real interior/piercing-in-progress photo but partially exposed midriff composition and heavy text overlay, dropped rather than risk an inappropriate crop), and all 12 Instagram Reel posters (permanent branded text baked into every frame, no clean crop available). The remaining 9 finished, healed, well-lit tattoo photos (bk-3, bk-7, bk-9, bk-10, bk-12, bk-13, bk-14, bk-15, bk-16) all had promotional text/logo overlays cropped out with PIL (kept only the real tattoo/skin region, verified visually after cropping) and were resized to max 1000px wide at quality 82.

notes: Discovery seed data (phone, IG handle, Facebook, address, Booksy URL, rating ballpark, no-own-website) was independently re-verified and confirmed correct via a fresh booksy_dossier.py run plus fresh IG API pull and web searches. Rating/review count refined to the exact Booksy JSON-LD values (4.9 rounded from 4.926829..., 41 reviews).
